mcpServers.title: MCP Servers
mcpServers.description: Connect any MCP-compatible tool server — a CRM, wiki, ticket system, automation platform, or a service you host yourself. Discovered tools become available to the task planner.
mcpServers.clientOnText: The assistant can use connected servers in any task that allows MCP data sources.
mcpServers.clientOffAdminText: Saved servers stay here, but the assistant will not call them until you turn this on for the installation.
mcpServers.clientOffUserText: An administrator needs to turn this on for the installation. Saved servers stay here until then.
mcpServers.clientEnabledNotice: The assistant can now call connected MCP servers
mcpServers.clientDisabledNotice: MCP calls are off — saved servers stay in place
mcpServers.clientUpdateFailed: Could not update the MCP setting
mcpServers.formHint: The URL must be a public HTTPS MCP endpoint (Streamable HTTP). The auth value is stored encrypted and never shown again.
mcpServers.emptyHint: Start from a blank form, or pick a known system to prefill the name and defaults. You can change or clear that choice at any time.
mcpServers.deleteMessage: Remove the connection "{name}"? The assistant will no longer be able to use its tools.
mcpServers.usageTitle: Which tasks may use these servers
mcpServers.usageDescription: Each task decides on its own whether the assistant may pull data from your connected servers while answering. Enable it for every task that should use them — for normal chat questions that is "General Chat".
mcpServers.usageNotUsedWarning: Your connected servers are not used yet: no task allows MCP data sources. Enable at least one task below, otherwise the assistant will never call these servers.
mcpServers.usageEnabled: MCP data sources enabled for this task
mcpServers.usageDisabled: MCP data sources disabled for this task
mcpServers.usageAdvancedHint: More options per task (server restrictions, instructions, models):
mcpServers.templatesHint: Custom is the default for any MCP server. A template only prefills the form — click the selected card again to clear it.

custom.name: Custom server
custom.hint: Paste the HTTPS URL of any Streamable HTTP MCP server and, if needed, an access token. CRM, wiki, tickets, automation — if it speaks MCP, it works here.

jira.name: Jira
jira.hint: Connect a Jira-capable MCP server (for example a self-hosted Atlassian MCP service) and paste its endpoint URL and access token. With write actions enabled, you can list tickets and create new ones from a prompt.

confluence.name: Confluence
confluence.hint: Connect a Confluence-capable MCP server (for example a self-hosted Atlassian MCP service) and paste its endpoint URL and access token. With write actions enabled, you can search pages, get summaries, and create new pages from a prompt.

github.name: GitHub
github.hint: Connect a GitHub-capable MCP server and paste its endpoint URL and a personal access token. Useful for issues, pull requests, and repository search.

n8n.name: n8n
n8n.hint: Connect an n8n MCP server so the assistant can inspect or trigger your automation workflows. Paste the MCP endpoint URL and access token from your n8n instance.

notion.name: Notion
notion.hint: Save the connection, then sign in with your Notion account. Synaplan can then search and read pages you grant access to. You can revoke access in Notion at any time.

higgsfield.name: Higgsfield
higgsfield.hint: Save the connection, then sign in with your Higgsfield account. Browsing your history is read-only; creating images or videos needs write actions and uses your Higgsfield credits.

mcpServers.oauthFormHint: This server uses your account sign-in. Save it, then you will be sent to the provider to allow access. No access token to paste.
mcpServers.disconnectMessage: The stored sign-in for "{name}" will be deleted. The server stays in your list — sign in again to use it.

aiAccounts.title: Your AI accounts
aiAccounts.subtitle: Use your own provider accounts instead of the server's. Keys are stored encrypted and only you can see them.

messagesGateway.title: Coding clients
messagesGateway.description: Connect Claude Code and other Anthropic-compatible agent tools to your Synaplan workspace. Requests go to POST /v1/messages and are metered against your Synaplan budget.
messagesGateway.setupHint: Point Claude Code at this Synaplan instance. Use exactly one credential variable — ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (x-api-key) or ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN (Bearer).
messagesGateway.keyHint: Stored encrypted for your account. Used when the gateway forwards requests to Anthropic.
messagesGateway.clearKeyConfirm: Remove key — coding clients use the server's key again if one is configured.
messagesGateway.byokPointer: Using your own Anthropic key? Manage it under Your AI accounts.
messagesGateway.webSearchLabel: Web search for connected AI assistants
messagesGateway.webSearchModePassthrough: Pass the request on to the AI provider
messagesGateway.webSearchHint: Automatic uses Synaplan's own search when a search provider is configured, and otherwise passes the request on to the AI provider.
messagesGateway.webSearchUnavailable: No search provider is configured on this instance, so requests are passed on to the AI provider. Only Anthropic can answer them.
messagesGateway.webFetchModePassthrough: Always pass web fetch to Anthropic
messagesGateway.webFetchHint: Synaplan does not download pages itself. On Anthropic models the gateway keeps or adds Anthropic's web_fetch tool so the model can open a URL. Other AI providers cannot run this tool.
messagesGateway.visionModePassthrough: Pass images on to the AI provider
messagesGateway.visionHint: Automatic uses Synaplan's vision model when the selected chat model cannot see images, and otherwise leaves images on the wire for the AI provider. Synaplan also offers an analyze_image tool for OCR.
messagesGateway.visionUnavailable: No Synaplan vision model is configured, so image turns are passed on to the AI provider. Configure a PIC2TEXT model under AI Models.
messagesGateway.upstreamWarning: All provider keys are sent to this host. Change only if you understand the risk.
messagesGateway.aliasesHint: Map the model names Claude Code asks for to models in your Synaplan catalog, for example claude-sonnet-4-6 → claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929.

settings.title: Gateway settings
settings.subtitle: These settings apply to every agent tool connected to this instance.
settings.disabledNotice: The gateway is off right now. Settings are saved and take effect as soon as you turn it on.

access.title: Access
access.description: Who can use the gateway, and which API key pays for the requests.

tools.title: Tool calling
tools.description: What connected AI assistants may do besides answering: use the tools of your workspace and search the web.

vision.title: Images
vision.description: How screenshots and other images are passed on to the AI provider. Agent tools resend every image of a session with each message, so these settings have a large effect on cost.

session.title: Context and session
session.description: What Synaplan adds to a request, and what it keeps afterwards.

connection.title: Connection
connection.description: Where requests are sent and how model names are translated.

activeTools.title: Running on your behalf right now
activeTools.empty: Synaplan runs no tools of its own. Connected AI assistants only get the tools their own program brings along.
activeTools.hint: A single message can still skip one of these: a program that brings its own tool of the same name keeps it, and web search only runs when the assistant asks for it.
activeTools.mcpServers: plus the tools of 1 connected tool server | plus the tools of {count} connected tool servers

enabled.label: Enable the gateway
enabled.description: While this is off, connected tools get a clear error instead of an answer.

operatorKey.label: Allow the instance key as fallback
operatorKey.description: Users without their own Anthropic key then use the key of this instance, and the cost counts against their Synaplan budget.

mcpTools.label: Let AI assistants use your tools
mcpTools.description: Synaplan runs the tools of your connected tool servers itself and passes the result back to the assistant.
mcpTools.noneConfigured: No tool server is connected yet. You can add one under Channels → MCP servers.

mcpWithClientTools.label: Offer your tools even when the agent tool brings its own
mcpWithClientTools.description: Claude Code already ships a full set of tools. Turn this on only if your own tools should be offered on top — a very long tool list makes an assistant less precise.

toolRounds.label: Maximum tool rounds per message
toolRounds.description: How often an AI assistant may use a tool and think again before it has to answer. Higher values allow more thorough work and cost more.

imageDetail.label: Image quality
imageDetail.description: How closely the AI model should look at an image. Low quality costs noticeably less and is usually enough to read text off a screenshot. Providers that do not offer this choice ignore it.

maxImages.label: Maximum images per message
maxImages.description: Only the newest images are sent; older ones are replaced with a note. This caps the cost of long sessions full of screenshots.

contextInjection.label: Add knowledge from your workspace
contextInjection.description: Synaplan adds matching information from your workspace to each request, so the AI assistant knows your context.

budgetNotice.label: Warn when the budget runs low
budgetNotice.description: The AI assistant receives a short note in its answer once your Synaplan budget is nearly used up.

sessionSummary.label: Keep a summary of each session
sessionSummary.description: Synaplan writes a short summary of every agent session to your chat history, so you can see later what was worked on.

settings.requiresMcpTools: Available once your tools are switched on above.
